title: dream-num/univer — The Office Harness for AI Agents — Spreadsheets, Docs, Slides, Canvas, Relational Tables, and PDF in one runtime.
content:
The Office Harness for AI Agents Spreadsheets · Documents · Presentations · Bases · Boards · PDFs (coming soon) High-performance, fully customizable Office SDK Build embeddable productivity experiences with a plugin architecture, Canvas-based rendering, a formula engine, and one Facade API that works in the browser and on Node.js. English | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Español 🌐 Website | 📖 Documentation | ✨ Showcase | 📘 API Reference | 📝 Blog Univer is an open-source SDK for creating office applications inside your own product. It gives you the building blocks for spreadsheet, document, and presentation experiences without forcing you into a hosted app or a fixed UI. Use Univer when you need to: - Embed spreadsheet or document editing into a SaaS product, internal tool, BI workflow, or AI application. - Run workbook/document processing on the server with the same architecture used in the browser. - Compose only the features you need through plugins or start quickly with presets. - Extend behavior through custom plugins, commands, services, UI components, and Facade APIs. Univer is not a spreadsheet file viewer only. It is a framework for building your own productivity surface. Across the Univer product family, Office tools share a runtime for storage and computation. Content can be composed and embedded across tools, with linked data and references updating together. People and AI agents can work in the same files. See the capability matrix for product coverage and Open Source and Pro for this repository's scope. These open-source projects are built with Univer Office SDK: Each project documents its own setup and SDK licensing requirements. - Isomorphic by design: run UI apps in browsers and headless processing in Node.js. - Plugin-first architecture: every capability is delivered as a composable plugin, so features can be added, removed, replaced, or lazy-loaded. - Preset mode for fast integration: use the curated plugin collections in presets/ when you want a working app quickly. - Plugin mode for full control: manually compose packages when you need custom loading, smaller bundles, or deep integration. - Facade API: work with workbooks, worksheets, ranges, documents, formulas, commands, and events through a higher-level API. - Canvas rendering engine: support large editable document surfaces with a rendering layer shared across document types. - Extensible UI: integrate with React, Vue, Web Components, and framework-specific application shells. Univer's AI and collaboration capabilities connect agent operations with interactive editing and human review: - Programmatic editing: agents inspect and modify Office content through structured APIs. - Output verification: agents check results through content inspection, rendered screenshots, and layout diagnostics. - Worktree collaboration: agents work in isolated drafts, then people review their changes and decide what to merge. See the AI SDK documentation for integration details. Live editing, shared revisions, and Worktree workflows require the corresponding Web SDK and collaboration capabilities; package availability and licensing vary by feature. Use Plugin Mode for complete product coverage and precise composition. For supported Sheets, Docs, and Node profiles, Preset Mode provides a shorter curated setup. report.summary: Univer is an open-source office SDK that gives AI agents and apps a single runtime for spreadsheets, docs, slides, and PDFs in browser or Node.js.
report.background: Most AI agents can write text but struggle to operate real business files. Spreadsheets in particular hold financial models, operations data, and planning logic that agents must read and edit reliably, yet existing options force a choice between heavyweight desktop suites, cloud APIs with limited structure, or fragile file-format parsers. Univer comes from the dream-num team, known for Luckysheet, and reframes the office editor as an embeddable SDK rather than a hosted product. Its pitch aligns with a broader 2024-2025 trend: as coding agents matured, vendors began exposing structured, verifiable interfaces for documents, design tools, and BI. Univer's answer is an isomorphic runtime where the same plugin graph, formula engine, and Facade API run in a browser tab and in a headless Node.js process, so agent-driven edits and human review happen on identical data structures.
key_points: One runtime, many surfaces: spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational bases, boards, and PDF support share a common storage and computation layer, so linked data and references update across formats instead of being siloed in separate file types.

Plugin-first and preset-fast: every capability ships as a composable plugin that can be added, removed, replaced, or lazy-loaded. Teams wanting a working app quickly use curated presets; teams needing smaller bundles or deep integration compose packages manually.

Canvas rendering plus a formula engine: a shared Canvas rendering layer targets large editable documents, while a dedicated formula engine handles spreadsheet computation, the piece agents most often need to evaluate rather than merely text-edit.

Agents get a verification loop: beyond programmatic editing via structured APIs, Univer advertises output verification through content inspection, rendered screenshots, and layout diagnostics, addressing the common failure mode where an agent writes data but cannot confirm it looks right.

Worktree-style collaboration: agents work in isolated drafts, and humans review proposed changes before merging, mirroring Git-style branching but applied to documents and workbooks, with live editing and shared revisions tied to the Web SDK.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Univer is a bet that office files become a first-class agent environment, similar to how code editors became the beachhead for coding agents. It gives vendors a self-hostable alternative to embedding Microsoft or Google surfaces, which matters for data-residency and vertical SaaS. For developers, the practical win is architectural: the same SDK runs in the browser and headless on Node.js, so an agent service and a human-facing editor share one code path, and the Facade API plus plugin overrides reduce the custom glue usually needed to bolt editing onto a product. For regular users, the visible change is likely indirect but meaningful: AI features inside the tools they already use could edit real spreadsheets and documents with reviewable, revertible drafts rather than one-shot generated files. Adoption still depends on ecosystem maturity, documentation quality, and how the open-source versus Pro licensing split lands for commercial embedding.
report.tools: Start with the dream-num/univer repo, then the @univerjs/presets packages for a fast sheets prototype and plugin mode when you need control. Read the AI SDK and Facade API docs for agent integration. Useful complements: HyperFormula or SheetJS for lightweight spreadsheet computation and file parsing, LibreOffice headless for conversion pipelines, Playwright for screenshot-based output verification, and Grist or NocoDB if you want a database-first spreadsheet rather than an embeddable SDK.
